rows.text: A token factory: anyone can create a named token, and accounts can transfer, approve, mint, burn or use a faucet. Visitors can read supply, balances and allowances, and list the tokens.
A profile store: an account can set its own text, number and yes-or-no profile fields, and anyone can read the fields of an account. It also renders a profile page.

A social realm with profiles, posts, replies, follows, likes, tips and creator tickets bought on a price curve. Visitors can read feeds, profiles and ticket quotes, and call the matching functions.

A game: players mint named fish, register them with a stake, and bite other fish to deal damage. Visitors can read each fish's owner, health and pool, and call Mint, Register, Leave and Bite.

An NFT platform ledger: creators can create and launch collections, mint tokens and reveal secrets, and engines can be registered. Visitors can read collections, tokens, traits, engines, fees and provenance.
An art engine adapter for the NFT platform: it can register its engine with the core realm, and readers can call its render and traits functions with an input value.
A read-only gallery for the NFT platform: its Render function shows the latest collections, one collection, one token, an engine or a user, as its package doc lists.

A fixed-price NFT market: token owners can list, reprice and cancel listings, and visitors can buy a listed token. Listings can be read by token, collection and seller, with a floor price per collection.
A minter for NFT collections: creators can create a collection, add sale phases and launch it, and visitors can mint tokens in an open phase. Price, phases and eligibility can be read.
A read-only JSON reader for the NFT platform: visitors can read gallery cards, trait counts, collections, a token's art and an address's profile in batches.

A read-only gallery page: it renders latest collections, a collection, a token with art, traits, owner and listing, an engine, and a user's collections and listings. It has no write functions.
A fixed-price NFT market: a token owner can list, reprice and cancel listings, anyone can cancel a stale one, and a buyer can buy a listing. Visitors can read listings and a collection's floor.
An NFT minting sale: a creator can open a collection, add sale phases, launch and reserve, and collectors can mint within a phase. Visitors can read prices, phases and whether an account is eligible.
A read-only JSON API for an NFT platform: it returns gallery cards, trait counts, a token's art, collections and an account's profile. It has no write functions.

An NFT collection with a built-in market: it is set up once, the creator grants minting rights, minters can mint, and tokens can be listed, delisted and bought. Visitors can read listings, tokens and recent sales.

A milestone escrow for client and freelancer contracts: a client can create and fund milestones, a freelancer can mark them delivered, and an admin can resolve disputes. Visitors can read contracts, counts and pause state.

An NFT badge collection: admins can mint quest and soulbound rank badges, update their metadata and burn them, and owners can approve and transfer quest badges. Visitors can read supply, owners and badge details.
An app directory: publishers can register app listings, curators can approve, reject or delist them, and users can flag a listing. Visitors can read listings by status or publisher, plus counts.
A game score leaderboard: allowlisted attesters can record scores and training receipts per game and day, and any account can stage a receipt request. Visitors can read boards, entries and receipts.

A governance bridge for a set of application realms: seated members can run admin actions on them once approved, pause them for a time, and hand admin to another account. Visitors can read each app's pause state.

A DAO discussion board with channels: the owner manages members and channels, members can post threads and replies, edit, delete and flag them, and admins can moderate. Visitors can read channels and threads.
A social feed: any account can post, reply, edit, delete, flag and react, and moderators can remove or restore posts. Visitors can read the feed, a user's posts, replies and counters.

A feedback discussion board with channels: the owner manages members and channels, members can post threads and replies, edit, delete and flag them, and admins can moderate. Visitors can read channels and threads.
A DAO governance core: seated members can propose actions, vote and execute roster changes, and governed realms consume approvals. Visitors can read the roster, proposals and policy constants.
A fee configuration for a marketplace: an admin can set a protocol fee per lane and the fee recipient, and hand admin over in two steps. Visitors can read a lane's fee and the recipient.

A quest completion record: anyone can submit a signed voucher to record a completion and its experience points, and the owner can rotate the signer key. Visitors can read an account's recorded quests and total points.

A review board: accounts can post, edit and delete ratings and comments on a subject, react and flag, and a moderator can hide items. Visitors can read reviews, comments, rating summaries and reputation.

An escrowed bounty board: posters create bounties with milestones, contributors apply and submit work, and reviewers approve or dispute it. Visitors can read counts, escrow totals and the board.
An escrow board for many-hands tasks: posters create campaigns with a fixed payout and slots, claimants submit claims, and reviewers approve or reject them. Visitors can read counts and campaigns.
An adapter from reputation scores to DAO membership: visitors can read tier thresholds, check an address for eligibility and render a portfolio, and an admin can set thresholds.
A ledger of completed work records and scores. Visitors can read scores, ranks, records and a leaderboard, while allowlisted writer realms add records and an admin curates the rules.
A club with invitation-based membership and single-choice polls. A visitor can read polls, members and rules, or call Invite, Join, CreatePoll, OpenPoll and Vote.
A contest where entrants submit entries through a form, reviewers accept or reject them, and members vote for a winner. It offers Submit, Accept, Reject, OpenVoting, Vote and Finalize.
A directory of entries submitted through a form and accepted or rejected by reviewers. A visitor can call Submit, or read the accepted entries, the review queue, members and rules.
A membership service whose member list other realms can read through RoleOf, Size and Snapshot. It also has Invite, Join, Leave, RemoveMember and SetRole for managing members.
A poll app whose voters come from a separate shared membership realm. A visitor can read polls, or call CreatePoll, OpenPoll, Vote and Finalize.
A penalty shootout game played against the chain. A visitor can call CreateGame, JoinGame, TakeShot, SubmitKeeperPlan and Forfeit, or read games and sessions as JSON.
The first rules engine behind the shots penalty game. It holds the game, kick and forfeit logic that the shots realm calls.
The second rules engine behind the shots penalty game. It keeps the game and kick logic and trims a finished shootout to a summary.
A penalty shootout rules engine for a game realm: it creates, joins, cancels and forfeits games, and plays shots and keeper plans. Visitors can read a game's required goal margin.

A registry of limited permissions that one address grants to another for a named realm function. A visitor can call Grant, Exercise and Revoke, or read Authorized, Get and Count.
A shared store of claims written as subject, predicate and object. A visitor can call ProposeClaim, SupportClaim, ContestClaim, AddEvidence, SupersedeClaim and ResolveClaim, or read a claim.
A review process where a fixed panel of jurors commits to hidden verdicts and then reveals them. A visitor can call OpenCase, Commit and Reveal, or read a case and its outcome.

A release tracker where version proposals collect reviews and a test result before they are approved. A visitor can call Propose, AddReview, AttestTests, Approve and Deprecate, or read the latest version.

A registry of agent identities that records registration, ownership transfers, operators and runtime changes. A visitor can call Register, Transfer, AddOperator and SetRuntime, or read an agent record.
An append-only log of execution receipts made of hashes, to which validators attach verdicts. A visitor can call Record and Attest, or read a receipt and its confirmation counts.
A message board with a fixed number of slots, where a post replaces the oldest one when full. A visitor can call Post, or read the latest messages, a topic, or messages since a sequence number.
A blog whose posts live in chain storage. A visitor can read the index, one post or a tag, and the realm has Set, Append, Delete and SetIntro for writing.
A shared settings store with notice banners and a pause switch that other realms read. A visitor can call Get, GetOr, Has, Keys and read the pause state.
A tiny demo with one function, Hello, that takes a name and returns a string.
A tiny demo that keeps a running total. A visitor can call Add with a number, which returns an integer.
A small generator that draws a face-like picture from a number. A visitor can call Draw with that number or read the rendered page.
A token demo that exposes its token for other contracts to read. A visitor can call MyBalance.
A tiny demo with one function, Hello, that returns a string.
A demo that shows a realm composing packages from another namespace. It keeps no state and renders a sample thread of posts.
A simple board of short text posts. A visitor can call CreatePost with a text and read the rendered list.
A small generator that draws a text picture for a chosen size. A visitor can call Draw with a size or read the rendered page.
A demo that renders greeting pages for a given name. A visitor can call Hello or read the rendered page.
A time-locked token vault demo. A visitor can call Deposit, Unvault, Redeem and Recover, or read MyBalance.
A simple token demo with balances per address. A visitor can call Mint and Send, or read BalanceOf.
A faucet that holds a balance and pays requests that approvers approve or deny. A visitor can call Request or Fund, or read Balance, Status and the request board.
A software forge that records repos, reference logs, issues, change requests and reviews. A visitor can call CreateRepo, OpenIssue, OpenChange and ReviewChange, or read repos and releases.
A curated gallery that lists art pieces from other realms and draws the ones it can import. A visitor can read the index or one piece, in markdown or plain text.
A registry that maps a deployed package path to the repository, commit and directory someone claims it came from. A visitor can call Register and Withdraw, or read HasClaims and OwnerClaim.
A name service that registers, renews and transfers names and stores records and subnames. A visitor can call Commit, Register, Renew and SetText, or read Resolve, OwnerOf and PrimaryName.

A grant board where requests with milestones are filed, members vote, and proofs are reviewed before tranches are released. A visitor can call Apply, ApplyFor, Fund and SubmitProof, or read the balance.
A greeting demo. A visitor can call Greet with a name, which records a greeting and returns it, or read Count of greetings.
A profile page assembled from named markdown slots. A visitor can read the page, the slot index or one slot with Get, and the realm has Set, Append and Delete for writing slots.
An account realm that approves modules with a grant and a budget, funds them and drives them. It has Claim, Approve, SetBudget, Revoke, Fund and Exec, and reads such as Address and SubAddress.
A store of slide decks kept as markdown, read as one page or slide by slide. A visitor can read the index or a deck, and the realm has Set and Delete for writing decks.
A reaction board where an address picks one fixed reaction for a page key. A visitor can call React and Unreact, or read Count, CountOf, Last and the embeddable reaction block.
A small text generator. A visitor can call Sapin with a size to get a string, or read the rendered page.
A minimal test realm that has only a Render page.
A directory of small utility realms, each listed with a title, description and tags. A visitor can read the directory or one tool, or call Slugs, PathOf, TitleOf, DescOf, Has and Tags.
A username lookup tool: visitors can resolve a name to an address or an address to a name, and check whether a name is current, canonical or already taken.
A vesting lookup: accounts can declare or remove their own vesting schedule, and visitors can read locked and spendable balances for an address and the declared schedules.
A demo realm combining developer packages: callers can add a short note or reset the list, and its page shows the notes, an author board and live chain values.
A read-only demo page that runs string algorithms such as soundex, rot13, pig latin and roman numerals on a word from the path, and compares two words. It stores nothing.
A constant-product market maker for pairs of GRC20 tokens: users add and remove liquidity, swap one token for another and move liquidity shares. Visitors can read pools, reserves, quotes and shares.
A storage demo board: callers can add entries, drop their own and compact dead nodes, and visitors can read fragmentation, reclaimable counts and a quote.
